title: Where should A stand for the shortest path?
description: Two corners sit three centimetres below a line, eight centimetres apart, and a third corner slides along the line. The video reflects one corner in the line, makes the path straight, and finds the smallest total length as ten centimetres. Keeko doubts that the spot straight above one corner is best.
teaching_notes: One idea: reflect one corner in the line, so the shortest path from B to the line to C becomes a straight line. Watch for students who pick the spot nearest to one corner.

source: B and C are 3 cm below line l and BC = 8 cm. Find the smalle
video_script.why: The child sees that reflecting one corner in the line turns the bent path B to A to C into a straight path, so the shortest total is a straight line.
video_script.substitution: the book's reflection in the line l; B and C both 3 cm below l and BC = 8 cm
video_script.anchor: the book's line l as a mirror, with B and C below it and the corner A sliding along l
video_script.wrong_answer: the best spot is straight above B
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko puts A straight above B because that makes A B the shortest it can be. The total A B plus A C is what matters, and A C becomes very long.
video_script.payoff_line: The smallest total is ten centimetres
maths_rules: reflect C in the line l to get C'; C is 3 cm below l, so C' is 3 cm above l, which is 3 + 3 = 6 cm above C
for every A on l, AC = AC', so AB + AC = AB + AC'
the shortest path from B to C' is the straight line BC', so the smallest AB + AC is BC'
BC' is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs BC = 8 and CC' = 6: BC' = √(64 + 36) = √100 = 10 cm
the straight line BC' crosses l halfway up, directly above the midpoint of BC, so A is on the perpendicular bisector of BC
check: A straight above B gives AB = 3 and AC = √(64 + 9) = √73 (about 8.54), total about 11.54 cm, which is more than 10 cm
video_script.design: One line and two corners all video. The line is a mirror, one corner is reflected, and the bent path becomes a straight one. Keeko's doubt: stand nearest to one corner.

narration: <bookmark mark='eq'/>Step two, the mirror keeps distances equal, so eigh C and eigh C prime are the same length.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The path B to eigh to C is as long as B to eigh to C prime.

beats.on_screen: shortest path from B to C′ is the straight line BC′; right triangle with legs 8 and 6: BC′ = √(64 + 36) = √100 = 10

<bookmark mark='tri'/>It is the long side of a right triangle with sides eight and six.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Sixty four plus thirty six is one hundred. The square root of one hundred is ten.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the smallest AB + AC is 10 cm, with A on the perpendicular bisector of BC
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The smallest total is ten centimetres.
